subject: MedBridge renewal: billing coverage window & PO timing orchestration
messages:
From: Sara Patel <procurement@medbridge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal timing and PO — Redwood renewal

Hi Aditya,

We're preparing the PO for our upcoming renewal with Redwood (RDW-4692). Two items we need to confirm before procurement can route to PO approval here:

1) Billing coverage if marketplace acceptance slips: our fiscal quarter cutover is 1/1/27. If acceptance on the Azure Marketplace (private offer) lags by 7–14 days, will Redwood provide a short 'billing coverage' window so we aren't double-billed or face a service interruption?

2) Preferred PO date vs. effective start date: our legal & finance prefer the PO to reflect the contract effective date (1/1/27), but Marketplace acceptance sometimes requires the offer to be active before that. Can you outline recommended timing (PO sign date, DocuSign send date, marketplace acceptance target) so we can schedule internal approvals?

We can circulate a draft PO once we confirm the acceptance window mechanics. Attaching our standard procurement checklist (not necessary to review now).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
MedBridge Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <procurement@medbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MedBridge renewal: billing coverage window & PO timing orchestration

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (finance/legal) and Karthik (marketplace ops) so we can give an operational timeline you can commit to. Quick answers up front:

- Short coverage window: yes, we can offer a 14-calendar-day coverage grace from your requested effective date to protect against marketplace acceptance delays. During that window we will hold existing pricing and capacity at the committed level; if acceptance slips past 14 days, we'll engage to either pro-rate or provide temporary credits depending on how long acceptance is delayed.

- Recommended sequence (we can adjust based on MedBridge's internal approvals):
  * Week 1: Redwood sends DocuSign (PO + standard SOW appendix).
  * Week 1–2: MedBridge signs PO and returns via DocuSign. 
  * Week 2: Redwood submits private offer to Azure Marketplace (takes 48–72h typical).
  * Target: Marketplace acceptance by no later than 14 days after your effective date; our 14-day coverage covers small slippage.

Attaching a draft PO for your intake team (MedBridge_PO_Draft_v3.pdf) — this uses our marketplace-ready language and includes a short clause describing the 14-day coverage and the 'soft rollback' path if the private offer is rejected by the marketplace.

Couple of asks:
- Kimberly/Karthik — please confirm the exact invoicing mechanics (invoice date vs start date) and whether Finance needs a separate credit memo flow documented.
- Sara — if you can indicate the approval cutoff date for routing PO internally (e.g., aim to have sign-off by 12/20), we can time the DocuSign send to match.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MedBridge_PO_Draft_v3.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MedBridge renewal: billing coverage window & PO timing orchestration

Thanks — quick internal note on finance/legal posture for MedBridge:

- Invoicing: we can invoice with an "invoice date" that matches the effective start (1/1/27) but will mark the invoice as contingent on marketplace acceptance if acceptance is outstanding. If acceptance is delayed within the 14-day window, we will not collect payment until acceptance is confirmed; instead we will issue a "provisional invoice" for internal tracking and then convert it to a final invoice once the offer is active.

- Credits / soft rollback: in the rare event the private offer is rejected after submission, Redwood will either supply (a) a one-time credit equal to the pro-rated amount for the gap period, or (b) extend capacity on the hosted API until the private offer is resolved — we prefer to resolve on a case-by-case basis. The clause in MedBridge_PO_Draft_v3.pdf covers this; if you need stronger binding language, let me know and Legal can produce a short amendment.

- Required fields for PO to avoid processing delays: exact billing address, tax ID, contact for last-mile billing questions, and preferred invoice delivery (SFTP/email). Please have MedBridge include those on the PO.

I'll review the SOW appendix once the updated capacity numbers are confirmed.

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: MedBridge renewal: billing coverage window & PO timing orchestration

Adding marketplace ops context (Azure private offer and multi-region capacity ramp):

- Typical timeline for Azure private offers is fast if the PO and offer content match the marketplace requirements: submit -> 48–72 hours for validation -> acceptance. Edge cases (tax/PO mismatch, billing address issues) add days because MSFT requests corrected PO via the buyer. That's the scenario our 14-day coverage guards against.

- Capacity uplift: MedBridge asked for a 20% reserved capacity uplift starting on day 1 of the renewal. We'll provision reserved nodes on our Dedicated pool upon acceptance. Ops needs the signed PO at least 7 business days before your desired provisioning date to schedule GPU allocation.

- SOW: I've attached a small workbook (SOW-accelerate-uplift.xlsx) with the node ramp schedule and recommended provisioning cutoffs. If MedBridge wants a hard guarantee for provisioning date, we should convert that to a signed amendment tied to the reserved capacity commit.

Karthik

Hi all — operations runbook and acceptance checklist below for clarity. Posting here so MedBridge procurement can map internal steps.

Acceptance runbook (Azure private offer):
1) Redwood prepares and sends the private offer payload to the Commerce Portal the same day PO is signed.
2) Azure validates buyer information; if there are mismatches they open a request for corrected PO to MedBridge (this is the main delay vector).
3) Once validated, Azure marks the private offer as accepted and the offer goes live in the buyer's tenant.

What Redwood will do for the 14-day coverage window:
- Hold pricing and reserved capacity at agreed-upon levels for up to 14 calendar days after the requested effective date.
- If marketplace acceptance is delayed beyond 14 days, Redwood will:
  * provide a pro-rated credit for days of missed reserved capacity OR
  * if MedBridge prefers, extend equivalent host-side capacity on the hosted API for the gap period while we continue to rectify the private offer.

Operational requests for MedBridge to avoid delays:
- Ensure the PO billing address/tax ID exactly match Azure marketplace billing records.
- Provide a single point of contact in IT who can respond within 24–48 hours to any marketplace validation queries (this prevents the 7–14 day escalations).

DocuSign & acceptance: once you confirm the internal approval cutoff, we'll queue DocuSign to match. We also created a DocuSign envelope draft for RDW-4692: https://www.docusign.net/medbridge/rdw4692 (draft).

I'll be on standby during acceptance window to triage Azure validation flags.

— Soojin Lee
Head of Marketplace Programs
Redwood Inference
